label: GO after a common-rewarded a2 trial, strongest trials 60-89, larger with S2 belief and a2 streak
terms: (phase == GO) * last_is("a2 S2 r") * (ep_dec == 6) ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a2 S2 r") * (ep_dec == 7) ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a2 S2 r") * (ep_dec == 8) ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a2 S2 r") * (ep_dec >= 5) * (ep_dec <= 8) * (tv("action", -2) == 2) * (tv("state", -2) == 2) * (tv("reward", -2) == 1) ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a2 S2 r") * (ep_dec >= 5) * (ep_dec <= 8) * (belief < 0.1) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_action == -1) * (belief < 0.2) * (ep_dec >= 6) * (ep_dec <= 8) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_action == -1) * (belief < 0.2) * (ep_dec == 5)
explanation: Fires only at GO (zero at D1 and D2). Magnitude is set by the previous trial being a2 -> S2 common and rewarded (the residual after other previous-trial patterns is about -0.09, i.e. near zero), gated by time in the episode. The a2-S2-r effect is near zero before trial 50, about +0.23 in trials 60-69, +0.44 in 70-79, +0.36 in 80-89, and drops again after 90. It grows further when the trial before was also a2 S2 r (+0.16) and when the ideal observer is confident S2 is good (belief < 0.1, +0.21). On the window first trial (previous trial unknown) it fires when belief < 0.2 in the same late-episode range. Upcoming choice and future reward are not needed. 7 observed-only terms: dev R^2 beyond timing 0.54, test 0.52. This is above the profile additive all ceiling (0.39) and all-observed (0.32), because the terms interact the previous-trial pattern with episode decile. The policy-decile reference alone scored 0.24, and observed belief plus history recovers that and more, so dropping model outputs loses essentially nothing here. Remaining error: peak activations (~1.2) in long a2 rewarded streaks are under-predicted (about 0.64 predicted).

issues: The factual claims hold up. Reproduced test R^2 beyond timing is 0.520. Every term pulls weight: dropping the trial -2 a2-S2-r term gives 0.510, dropping the belief<0.1 term gives 0.506, and the three (a2 S2 r x decile) terms alone give 0.418. The activation is GO-only and the profile's residuals at D1 and D2 are 0.

A large systematic error class remains. On GO steps after every previous-trial pattern other than 'a2 S2 r' (a1 S1 r/u, a1 S2 r/u, a2 S2 u, a2 S1 r/u), misses shows the model over-predicting by about 0.073-0.078 (e.g. GO after a2 S2 u -0.078, GO after a1 S1 r -0.076). The explanation says the activation is close to zero after other patterns, but the terms never encode that. Those steps keep the timing baseline (up to 0.28 in deciles 6-8), so the mean error at GO is -0.039 and at D1/D2 it is +0.020. Adding one term, (phase==GO)*(prev known)*(not a2 S2 r)*time-profile, lifts test R^2 from 0.520 to 0.694 with the original terms. With a reworked 8-term set it reaches 0.712 test / 0.723 dev, and the per-phase mean errors drop to about 0.

'Drops again after trial 90' is overstated. The worst misses are decile-9 windows that are still in long rewarded a2 runs: actual 0.98, 0.91, 0.82, 0.71 at t89-92 against predicted 0.02-0.23. The activation decays gradually through trials 90+ rather than switching off. An (ep_dec==9)*(99-ep_trial) term adds a little (0.532).

Other systematic misses: windows that start mid-streak (prev_action == -1) with actual about 1.15-1.2 are predicted about 0.10. This is because the belief term, computed without the earlier history, is weak. Some streaks that follow an unrewarded trial build up slowly (actual 0.17-0.28 against predicted 0.8-1.0).

The statement that 'explaining it without the model's policy loses essentially nothing' compares hand-built interaction terms (0.52) with a single additive policy-decile table (0.24). Those numbers are not comparable, so they say nothing about what is lost by leaving out the model's own outputs.
